Load 2: the view origin, column $00 and row $0A in characters. The screen builder $6D17 halves them at $6D26 and $6D2B to find the first metatile to draw; $6D8B–$6DA0 copies them to the left and top view bounds and computes right and bottom by adding $25 and $12 modulo 256; $6DA3–$6DBE scrolls once more down or right for an odd row or column; and $6DC1–$6DD6 stores the final bounds, adding $26 and $13. $33EC–$3408 saves both bytes, puts the current view's left and top ($569B, $569D) there for $6D17 to redraw the screen, and restores them.
The little-endian address $BF4F of this load’s entity records. $1863 copies it into the pointer at $E2–$E3.

The initial entity-slot limit is 5. $186D copies it to $4DBA, which bounds the slots that entity records fill: the initializer at $1863 loads records into slots 1 to 5 ($18CB). The load has 5 entity records, all of which the initializer loads, stopping at the zero byte after them; each pass, the slot scan at $3622 checks slots 1 to 5 ($3629), and since no record follows, $3632 finds that zero byte and reloads an empty slot's own record at $366A.

A 256-byte lookup indexed by screen character value: entry N is the colour-RAM byte for character N. After $6D17 draws the 20-by-10 metatile map window, it jumps to $6F3E, whose loop at $6F59–$6F5F reads each character of that screen buffer and writes the corresponding table byte to colour RAM, 39 columns by 20 rows from $D8C8. The view-shift routines read the table the same way for the column or row a scroll exposes: $30E1 for the right column, $319C for the left column, $3256 for the bottom row and $3314 for the top row. The visual-selector screens take their colours from the tables at $7F9E/$7FA5 instead, through $70ED. The table continues across $8000.
Continuation of the character-to-colour lookup beginning at $7FCF; this byte is entry $31 of that table, and entries continue through $80CE.

A 256-byte attribute table indexed by the map's metatile value. The player's downward check tests bits 0–1 at $0C57 and, for the next column, at $0C7A; the player's horizontal checks at $0EB8 and $1051 test bit 1 when clipping the player against a tile. For entities, the downward scan at $450C tests bits 0–1 at $4532 and $4542, and the horizontal test at $460C reads four attributes through $4632 (at $464C), keeping bit 1 of the first two and bit 0 of the last two.

A 256-byte table of top-left character codes indexed by a metatile value. The full-screen draw loop at $6D4D writes the selected code to the first cell of a two-by-two screen block. The scroll routines $2C8D, $2D82, $2E77 and $2F45 read it through a pointer when they draw a newly exposed column or row: they point ($58) at $2D02 (scrolling right) and $2DF7 (left), for a column of left halves, and at $2EF0 (down) and $2FCB (up), for a row of top halves.

A 256-byte table of top-right character codes indexed by a metatile value. The full-screen draw loop at $6D53 writes the selected code to the cell to the right of the first cell. The scroll routines $2C8D, $2D82, $2E77 and $2F45 read it through a pointer when they draw a newly exposed column or row: they point ($58) at $2CF1 (scrolling right) and $2DE6 (left), for a column of right halves, and ($5A) at $2EF0 (down) and $2FCB (up), for a row of top halves.

A 256-byte table of bottom-left character codes indexed by a metatile value. The full-screen draw loop at $6D5A writes the selected code to one 40-character screen row below the first cell. The scroll routines $2C8D, $2D82, $2E77 and $2F45 read it through a pointer when they draw a newly exposed column or row: they point ($5A) at $2D02 (scrolling right) and $2DF7 (left), for a column of left halves, and ($58) at $2EDF (down) and $2FBA (up), for a row of bottom halves.

A 256-byte table of bottom-right character codes indexed by a metatile value. The full-screen draw loop at $6D60 writes the selected code to one row below and one cell to the right of the first cell. The scroll routines $2C8D, $2D82, $2E77 and $2F45 read it through a pointer when they draw a newly exposed column or row: they point ($5A) at $2CF1 (scrolling right) and $2DE6 (left), for a column of right halves, and at $2EDF (down) and $2FBA (up), for a row of bottom halves.

They lie beyond the map’s 16 rows, the count at $7F4C. Save X and Y in immediate operands, call $36E9 to split A into nibbles plus one, clear the first two bytes at $B283, and write the tens and units codes to the next two bytes. A tens code of 1 is written as zero. Restore Y, call the digit drawer at $B22A, restore X and return.

The incoming N and Z flags select the path: negative enters the first-price balance check at $AF9E; zero selects a message at $AFEC; otherwise use the second-price path at $AF70. The only jump here is $B158, straight after LDA $B289, so the flags are those of the shop selection byte.

Reached from $AF6C when the shop selection byte is 1. Load X from $7B and call $78D1 with stage field $4789,X, record byte 9, the second price: $78D1 subtracts it in packed decimal from the selected player’s gold and restores the gold if that borrows. Load 2: multiply item ID A by eight with eight-bit wrap, split the two packed bytes from the item table at $B5DF into four nibble-plus-one values at $B283, and replace consecutive leading ones with zero. Nibbles and item indexes are not locally validated.

Load 2: mutable shop selection byte. The input loop initializes it to zero, left and right paths update it, and the cursor helper indexes the position table using this value plus one.

Load 2: five item-index offsets, $00, $00, $0D, $00 and $06, at $B290–$B294. Three zero-terminated glyph lines, with alignment spaces omitted here: “Welcome!” / “May I help you?” / “”, then the control byte $20.
